SMTEC Rater Handbook
Revised 21 October 2026 (B.E. 2569)
For expert raters

You are one of the independent raters in a held-out validation of the SMTEC instrument. You will receive a blinded workbook containing claims from sustainability reports, an evidence pack of related passages for assessing each claim, and columns for your scores.
1. What SMTEC measures

SMTEC scores the substantiation of SDG-related claims in corporate sustainability reports. A well-substantiated claim is supported by information that is sufficient, appropriate and verifiable. Such information helps confirm that the claim is as worded, that it covers the whole scope of the claim, and that it is enough for a reader who wants to check the claim or hold the company to it, for example analysts or investors, assurers, regulators, civil society organisations or the media, and lenders.
SMTEC has 5 dimensions, each scored from 0 to 3. You will score S, M, T and E. The research team will compute C from the passage labels you give (Section 6). The dimensions are defined as follows:
S (Specificity): does the claim name the organisation, programme, group, community, area or scope?
M (Measurability): does the claim give figures, a baseline and a target?
T (Temporality): does the claim give a point in time or a period?
E (Evidence): does the claim state a method, a source, or certification/assurance?
C (Corroboration): do other parts of the report contain verifiable facts or additional information related to this claim? (Repetition does not count.)
2. Scoring principles

2.1 You are scoring the claim, not the organisation. SMTEC does not measure whether the claim is true, whether the company actually did it, or whether the company contributes to any SDG. A claim may be fully supported by evidence in the report and still be false (written in the report but not actually done). Conversely, a true claim may have no supporting evidence in the report (actually done but not written in the report). Scoring therefore rests only on what the report discloses.

2.2 Read only the information given in the workbook. Do not read other outside evidence (for example news, ratings, or personal knowledge of the company). If you happen to know something about the company, please do not use it in your scoring.
2.3 Do not judge intent. Words such as symbolic, greenwashing, over-claiming and under-claiming describe behaviour; they are not scores and should not be written in the comment column.

4. Scoring steps
Please work in this order:
4.1 Score S, M and T from the claim text (claim_text) only. Do not read the evidence pack.

4.2 Score E by reading the claim together with the whole evidence pack, both same-section (S1, S2) and cross-section (X1 to X3), looking for the method of data collection, the reporting scope, the source, the standard used, or the name of the certifier. (E assesses the quality of the evidence, not the number of passages.)
4.3 Give a label to every passage slot (S1, S2, X1 to X3), one passage at a time, using the definitions in Section 6.
4.4 Write a comment if any condition in Section 7 applies.
5. Scoring the SMTEC dimensions

Scoring rule: scores must be whole numbers 0, 1, 2 or 3. No half points and no blanks. If you cannot decide, choose the lower score (for example, if you hesitate between 2 and 3, choose 2) and write a comment saying which scores you could not decide between.
5.1 Specificity (S)
Read the claim and ask: how specific is the information in this claim?
Note: figures (e.g. "500 employees") belong to dimension M and do not raise S.
5.2 Measurability (M)
Read the claim and ask: how far does this claim give quantitatively measurable information?
5.3 Temporality (T)
Read the claim and ask: does this claim state a time or a period?

Note: "completed", "achieved" or "installed" without a date scores 1, not 0, because completion refers to a time in the past. A single time point (e.g. "by 2030") scores 2. A score of 3 requires at least two time points that allow progress to be tracked (a base year and a target year, or a target year and interim milestones).
5.4 Evidence (E)

Read the claim together with the evidence pack (S1, S2, X1 to X3) and ask: for this claim's data, does the report state how the data were obtained, a source, a standard, or certification by an external body?
Notes:

Naming a standard without its number (e.g. "in line with GRI") scores 1. It scores 2 if at least one of the following is also given: (a) the scope of the data or the standard's number, i.e. what the data cover, such as the specific disclosure (GRI 305 or GRI 305-1), the units or areas covered (all plants in Thailand), or the period (2024); or (b) the location of the data in the report, i.e. where the figure is, such as a page, a table, or the GRI content index entry that refers to these data.
"Independently verified" or "certified by a third party" without naming the certifying organisation scores 2.
A named certifier (audit firm, certification body) or a named certification standard (e.g. ISO 14064) that is tied to the data of this claim scores 3.
Evidence that is not in the evidence pack must not be considered in scoring.
5.5 Corroboration (C) ***You do not need to do this part

You do not enter a C score. The research team computes C from the labels you give to X1 to X3 (Section 6), by counting how many different sections of the report the passages labelled Extend come from. This section explains the calculation so that you understand the effect of the Extend label.
If several passages labelled Extend come from the same section, they count as 1 section (1 point only).
Passages labelled Redundant, Related or Unrelated do not count towards the score.
Passages labelled Contradicts are not counted and no points are deducted, but the research team records that the passage conflicts with the claim.

If X1 to X3 contain no passages (all None), C = 0, and the research team records separately that "no passage was available to check". This differs from the case where passages exist but are Unrelated.
S1 and S2 are not counted in C.
6. Passage labels

Give a label to every passage in the evidence pack (S1, S2, X1 to X3), one at a time, by comparing it with the claim's specific content (figures, programme name, scope or area, target, or dates). Choose one value per passage:
Judge by the content of the passage compared with the claim, not by its length or by the number of repeated words.
If you hesitate between Extend and Redundant, ask: "Does this passage give any information beyond the claim itself?" If not, choose Redundant and write a comment.
Example. Claim: "Reduced water use at the Rayong plant by 12% in 2024 against the 2022 base year."
Extend: environmental data table "Water use, Rayong plant: 2022 = 1.25 million m3; 2024 = 1.10 million m3" (gives the figures to check the 12% reduction).
Redundant: executive summary "In 2024 we cut water use by 12%" (repeats; adds no fact).
Related: "The company places importance on sustainable water resource management" (same topic, but does not address the 12% reduction at Rayong).
Unrelated: "The company provided safety training to 1,200 employees".
Contradicts: "The Rayong plant reduced water use by 8% in 2024 compared with 2022" (a different figure for the same indicator and period).
Examples of passages that should be labelled Contradicts:
Several different figures for the same indicator and the same period.
"Zero waste to landfill", while a landfilled waste quantity other than 0 is reported.
Different target years in different parts of the report (e.g. one part says 2030, another says 2035).
Scope that conflicts with itself (e.g. "all sites" in one place, but "two pilot sites" in another part).
7. Notes and rules
Score the rows in the order they appear in the file. Do not sort or filter rows.

Score each item once. Do not go back to "adjust" an earlier row after seeing more items. If you feel your scoring standard has changed, please write a comment at the row where you noticed it, and continue to the end.
Write a comment when:
you hesitate between two scores, e.g. between 2 and 3;
the evidence pack has no passages, or you consider that it has no passage related to the claim;
the claim text is cut off, cannot be understood, or appears to be two claims merged.
Do not describe the organisation's behaviour in the comment column, e.g. that the organisation is greenwashing.
Do not edit locked columns.
Do not discuss individual claims with other raters until all workbooks have been returned.
8. How your scores will be used

Your scores will be compared with those of the other raters to assess agreement and consistency among human raters, before they are compared with the scores of the multi-agent framework developed in this study.
Your passage labels will also be used to check whether the passages retrieved by the instrument are actually related to the claim.
